name: Oil & Natural Gas Corporation Ltd (ONGC)
tagline: India's largest upstream E&P company at a trough valuation (~7x P/E, ~5.6% dividend yield) and a genuine beneficiary of the domestic drilling/exploration-capex cycle, but a ~Rs 3 lakh Cr PSU whose size forecloses the 10x/100x mandate and whose production has been broadly flat for a decade.
business_overview: State-controlled integrated oil & gas major: ~two-thirds of India's domestic crude and gas production, plus downstream (HPCL, MRPL), overseas E&P (ONGC Videsh) and a gas-marketing arm. Upstream day-rates, rig utilisation and exploration commitments drive the entire domestic oilfield-services chain, which is the reason it was seeded (theme-scan 2026-09-09, user-authorised 1x no-self-discovery bypass; oilfield-services / drilling & exploration-capex theme). ONGC is the bellwether that sets that capex, not a small proxy that levers off it.
fundamentals_table: ~7% revenue CAGR; production broadly flat for years
Gross debt ~Rs 1.7 lakh Cr, cash ~Rs 0.5 lakh Cr; leveraged but serviceable for a PSU of this cash generation
fundamentals_narrative: Cheap, cash-generative and undemanding on valuation - nothing about an oil-capex re-rating is priced in. But the numbers that matter for this screen are the ones that cap the outcome: ~Rs 3 lakh Cr market cap (10x would be larger than the entire current Nifty energy complex), single-digit volume growth, a windfall-tax overhang that swings with crude, and capital tied up in downstream stakes. ROCE ~14% is respectable for the sector but not a compounding engine. This is a yield-plus-modest-upside PSU, not a multi-bagger.
technical_read: Not pulled - near the lower half of a tight 52-week band is known; the assessment turns on size math, not the chart.
sentiment_summary: No dedicated ONGC ValuePickr thread resolved with confidence (search across categories 11/14/17 returned only tangential threads - Petronet, Jindal Drilling, Alphageo). topic_slug left null. Assessment is web/fundamentals-based, which is appropriate for a widely-covered large-cap PSU.
community_signal: No trusted-user activity found. Broker view on the sector is 'cheap, crude-linked, windfall-tax risk'.
bse_notes: No SEBI/fraud action. Windfall tax on domestic crude (reviewed fortnightly) is a recurring policy overhang for the whole upstream PSU group. Government is the majority owner and periodically uses ONGC for policy purposes (subsidy sharing, cross-holdings).
bull_case: ~7x earnings, ~0.8x book, ~5.6% dividend yield - almost nothing priced in
Genuine leverage to higher crude/gas prices and to any pick-up in domestic exploration & development activity (KG-98/2 ramp, new OALP rounds)
Largest reserves base and infrastructure in India; national-champion status
bear_case: ~Rs 3 lakh Cr market cap - 10x/100x is arithmetically implausible; fails the screen's return-magnitude bar on size alone
Production broadly flat for a decade despite heavy capex; reserve replacement a chronic concern
Windfall-tax regime caps the upside from crude spikes
Capital allocation constrained by government ownership (downstream stakes, subsidy sharing)
PSU governance discount is structural, not closing
verdict_headline: Cheap, crude-linked large-cap PSU and a real oilfield-capex bellwether, but size math forecloses the 10x/100x mandate and there is no specific named structural or management inflection to invoke the large-cap exception. thesis_fit 'neither', conviction Low-Medium.
verdict_reasoning: four_box: tailwind weak (higher crude/gas prices and a domestic E&P capex uptick are real but cyclical, not a structural multi-year growth engine; production flat), tam no (genuine large-cap - a ~Rs 3 lakh Cr company cannot deliver the required multiple), moat yes (largest reserves/infrastructure base in India, national upstream champion), valuation yes (~7x P/E, ~0.8x book, ~5.6% yield - the thesis is not priced in) -> score 2.5

Score 2.0-2.5 with the valuation box = yes technically permits a return-magnitude label, but this is a genuine large-cap and there is NO specific named management or structural inflection (a turnaround CEO, a regulatory regime change, a capital-allocation shift) - only 'cheap + crude optionality'. Size math is a legitimate 'neither' here; label kept at 'neither'.

Conviction Low-Medium: undemanding valuation and a real (if modest) crude/capex tailwind put it above Low, but flat production, the windfall-tax overhang and PSU capital-allocation keep it below Medium

Seeded via the oilfield-services / drilling & exploration-capex theme (external lead, user-authorised bypass) - ONGC IS the bellwether that drives that theme's capex, not a levered proxy; no value_chain block written (position is self-evident: upstream operator at the head of the chain)
No red flag tier (solvent, profitable, dividend-paying PSU)

four_box.note: tam = no on genuine large-cap size math (~Rs 3 lakh Cr); tailwind weak because the crude/capex driver is cyclical not structural and production has been flat. Valuation undemanding and reserve/infra moat real, but no named inflection to lift the label off 'neither'.
